what: round 4 study sbi (track 2): simulate-to-train on the gliders wind world with 4 hidden parameters (lR, dm_00, ls_00, lh): synthetic-likelihood identification from budgeted Lab data, then level-1 predictors trained on real data vs simulations

identification.method: Gaussian synthetic likelihood on 4 linear-regression summaries per episode (mean over the budget's episodes); cubic emulator + emulator and CV-misfit covariance; importance sampling under the viability prior p_v

offline_calibration.what: held-out design points (uniform on the box), projection + emulator refit on the other 80%, posterior from the point's own first n episodes under a flat box prior
offline_calibration.platform: CPU (this container), deterministic from r4-sbi-002 design_features.npz

conclusions: Identification: Gaussian synthetic likelihood on 4 regression summaries contracts all 4 parameters already at 2 episodes (66 ticks; posterior sd / prior sd 0.17-0.44) and to 0.06-0.12 at 512 episodes; contraction flattens beyond about 128 episodes: 128 -> 512 episodes shrinks the sd by only 0.84-0.97x (checker), because the emulator and CV-misfit covariance, which do not shrink with n, dominate the likelihood there (a floor by construction of the method; on average it is conservative at these truths: the Lab summaries' chi2 at the true theta under the data-only covariance is 49 at n = 512 against 94 expected from the misfit model). Marginal coverage is close to nominal on 8 truths (in50 0.34-0.56, in90 0.875-1.0; 32 checks per budget, correlated within truths and nested across budgets) and on 300 held-out design points at n <= 4 (in50 0.50-0.52, in90 0.89-0.90); the joint 90% HPD covers 6/8 truths at n = 128 and 512; at n = 512 truth 4 (dm_00 near the box edge, u = -0.87) lies at HPD level 0.9997 (chi2 of its Lab summary at the true theta 21 under the full likelihood covariance, 4 expected), one clear miss, larger than the constant misfit term allows; 8 truths cannot measure the rate (checker). The offline check uses simulator episodes only, so it tests the inference machinery, not simulator-vs-Lab agreement. See identification.per_budget, identification.offline_calibration.

Prediction: the net trained on 1,024 simulated episodes at posterior draws matches the net trained at the true parameters at every budget (true - post within +-0.003 OES, |z| <= 1.03), even at 2 episodes; for the ridge, 2 episodes leave 0.010 (item z 3.0, truth-cluster z 1.8, 6/8 truths) and 8 or more match. The same net on the real Lab data needs 512 episodes to come within 0.019 OES (z 5.8) and is far worse below (gap post - real 1.04 / 0.52 / 0.22 / 0.10 / 0.019 at 2 / 8 / 32 / 128 / 512 episodes; truth-cluster z 8.1 / 10.6 / 13.5 / 13.6 / 4.5, 8/8 truths each). The size of this gap is learner-specific (checker): the real@2 net trains on one episode (the other is its early-stopping hold-out); the ridge on real data reaches 0.387 at 8 and 0.458 at 32 episodes (equal to the net's real@128, 0.459) and comes within 0.006 (truth-cluster z 1.4) of its simulation-trained version at 128 episodes and level at 512 (-0.003). Simulation training beats real-data training at every budget for the net, and up to 32 episodes for the ridge. At 512 the net compares 1,024 simulated with 512 real episodes, so data source and amount are confounded. See prediction.table, prediction.headline_gaps.

Most of the gain is knowing the simulator, not identifying theta: a net trained on prior-predictive simulations (no real data) scores 0.544, equal to real@512 (gap +0.002, z 0.4); identification adds 0.021 OES on top (net true - prior_pred, item z 5.7, truth-cluster z 3.4, 8/8 truths; ridge 0.042, z 7.7, cluster z 5.9; amortised net 0.030, cluster z 5.2); the box-centre plug-in loses 0.091 (net; cluster z 3.3) against the truth. Box centre is worse than prior-predictive training for the net (0.070, cluster z 2.8) and the ridge (0.036, cluster z 2.3) but not for the amortised net (0.002, cluster z 1.6). The prior_mean and prior_pred nets are one trained net each, shared by all 8 truths, so no z here includes their training-seed variance (checker). See prediction.extra_gaps, prediction.headline_gaps.

Checker addition: the amortised theta-conditioned net (8,192 design episodes, 6,000 steps) beats the per-theta nets (1,024 episodes, 3,000 steps) by 0.007-0.012 OES (item z 2.2-4.2, truth-cluster z 1.3-2.9; at 32 episodes not significant); data and steps differ 8x and 2x, so this does not isolate amortisation. 46 of 50 simulation-trained nets (and the amortised net) had their best held-out loss at the last or second-to-last evaluation, so about 0.575 is not shown to be a ceiling for history-only predictors, and the remaining gap to the oracle mixes level-0 state uncertainty with predictor limits; the study shows only that the parameters account for about 0.02-0.04 of it (true - prior_pred: net 0.021, amortised 0.030, ridge 0.042). See checker.

checker.who: independent checker of round-4 study sbi (worktree wt-sbichk), 8 Nov 2026; no GPU job run; about 5 CPU-minutes (nice 10)
checker.verdict: the code does what the report says; every OES, gap, identification and calibration number recomputes from the saved outputs; job records match; no secret committed. The direction of every main conclusion holds with truth-clustered uncertainty. Wording overstated in places: 'beats real-data training at every budget' holds for the net, not for the ridge beyond 32 episodes; '2 episodes match the true parameters' holds for the net, not quite for the ridge; the size of post - real at small budgets is specific to a data-only net trained on 1-7 episodes; the 128 -> 512 contraction is 0.84-0.97x, not 0.8x; one truth is a clear coverage miss at 512; z values are item-level; 'remaining gap = state uncertainty' and 'amortisation helps' are not isolated. prior_mean is the box centre (SL.CEN, u = 0); prior_pred draws theta from the viability-weighted box; each is one net (and one ridge) shared by all 8 truths.

Nets keep their best held-out-episode parameters (val_frac 0.1, at least 1 episode): real@2 trains on 1 episode (94 examples), real@8 on 7; sim nets on 922 of 1,024 episodes; train_info.json best_step is 2,750 or 3,000 of 3,000 for 46 of 50 simulation nets and 6,000 of 6,000 for the amortised net.

Synthetic likelihood: covariance Sigma(u)/n + v(u) Sigma_mean + Bm; the last two do not shrink with n, so the contraction floor is built in. Offline calibration uses simulator episodes at held-out design points (flat box prior), so it checks the inference, not simulator-vs-Lab agreement.
OES SEs are an iid bootstrap over the 512 pooled items (vw.scoring.skill_report); they ignore the 8-truth clustering and the per-truth training of each net.

report_wording_not_in_summary: Headline 'beats one trained on the real Lab data at every budget': net only; ridge real >= post at 512 (-0.003) and post - real 0.006 (cluster z 1.4) at 128.
'Two episodes of identification already match the true parameters': net only; ridge true - post@2 = 0.010 (cluster z 1.8, 6/8 truths).
'four times the data shrinks the sd by only 0.8x': 0.84, 0.97, 0.88, 0.88 (lR, dm_00, ls_00, lh).
'joint 90% region misses 2 of 8 ... mild overconfidence': at 512 one miss is far out (truth 4, HPD level 0.9997); marginal in90 is 0.97-1.0, so the misses are joint, not marginal.
'learning from data alone needs about 512 episodes': for this net; the ridge on 32 real episodes equals the net on 128.
'Amortised net 0.574-0.575 at posterior draws': 0.5735-0.5752 (0.573-0.575 at 3 decimals); its edge over the per-theta nets is confounded with 8x data and 2x steps (cluster z 1.3-2.9).

'remaining gap to the oracle is uncertainty about the state, not the parameters': only the second half is shown (parameters about 0.02-0.04); predictor limits are not separated from state uncertainty.

'partly revises the round-3 finding': round 3's ridge gap (true - box centre 0.063, item z 1.3, 4 truths, 4 x 60 training ticks) was underpowered; the new 0.079 (cluster z 4.3) has the same sign and size, so it resolves rather than reverses it.

All z in the report are item-level; truth-cluster z are 1.2-4.6x smaller (truth_clustered_gaps); the direction of every main conclusion survives with cluster z >= 2.2 (smallest: ridge box centre vs prior predictive 2.3, 7/8 truths; ridge post - real at 2 episodes 2.9, 8/8 truths).
